fields.v: LLMoxie (three-tier institutional AI platform: inference layer, LiteLLM/MLflow control plane, application augmentation layer) and RSE-Plugins (open-source Plugin-Agent-Skill hierarchy for Claude Code: Scientific Python Development, Scientific Domain Applications, AI Research Workflows, Project Management plugins). No versions

AI Research Workflows plugin: structured markdown research findings in .agents/; implementation plans with phased units and measurable success criteria (automated and manual checks); experiment, implementation and handoff templates; structured validation report. Other plugins: agents, skills, slash commands; community health files (README, CONTRIBUTING, CITATION.cff, etc.)

Six phases with slash commands: (1) Research (/research), (2) Planning (/plan), (3) Plan iteration (/iterate-plan), (4) Experimentation (/experiment, optional), (5) Implementation (/implement, phase-by-phase with verification checkpoints), (6) Validation (/validate, automated checks + manual testing steps + validation report)
Plan iteration on user feedback; planning is 'interactive'; manual checks listed in plans and identified at validation; otherwise Not stated
Not run as a study (approach described; used in practice in the center's projects, no measured evaluation)

Not stated in Böckeler's terms; authors cite spec-driven development: research phase 'enables a spec-driven development workflow where specifications become executable, directly generating working implementations' (spec-first, plan-centred)

rev.why: The authors' wording ('specifications become executable, directly generating working implementations') reads like spec-as-source, but the described flow (research notes and plans in .agents/ feeding one implementation) looks spec-first; no statement on keeping specs after implementation. Could also be 'not classifiable'.

Only one sentence (p. 5) mentions SDD: 'specifications become executable, directly generating working implementations' (spec-as-source wording), while the described flow (research notes and plans in .agents/ consumed by one implementation, then validation) reads as spec-first. Nothing says whether specs are kept or maintained afterwards; 'not classifiable' is also defensible.
